hero.lead: A young nation of 1.4 million whose Petroleum Fund held $18.43 billion at the end of June 2026, about nine times its non-oil economy on IMF figures, while only one Timorese in five cooks with clean fuel.

capital.heading: A sovereign fund that must outlast the oil.

register.name: Petroleum Fund of Timor-Leste
register.detail: Central Bank of Timor-Leste · Quarterly report, 30 June 2026
register.text: The nation’s savings from oil and gas, invested abroad and drawn on by Parliament for each budget.

register.name: Dili Water Supply Project
register.detail: World Bank · approved 25 May 2022 · project P176687 · principal US$121,000,000
register.note: An older instrument, approved in 2022; World Bank commitments to Timor-Leste total US$354.5 million across 16 IBRD and IDA projects (31 October 2026)
register.text: World Bank financing of US$121 million for the water supply of Dili, the capital. It serves the water standard: 87.3% of Timorese have basic drinking water, and safely managed water is not yet measured.

register.name: Coffee and Agroforestry Livelihood Improvement Project, additional financing
register.detail: ADB · approved 26 June 2026 · $4 million grant from the Asian Development Fund · $950,000 grant from the Green Climate Fund, Community Resilience Partnership Program
register.note: Extends support to between 2,000 and 4,000 farming households in six municipalities
register.text: Grant financing that scales up farmer training and resilient agroforestry, coffee quality and marketing, adaptation to climate shocks and livelihood support for women and youth. It serves the food and livelihood standards: 53.7% of Timorese are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Workforce Skills Development Project
register.detail: ADB · grant agreement signed in Dili 12 December 2025 · Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific
register.note: Priority trades include construction, automotive and mechanics
register.text: A grant, administered by ADB and funded by Japan, that improves teaching and learning at selected technical and vocational institutions and aligns curricula and certification with the needs of industry, with fair access for women and marginalised groups. It serves the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Dili West Water Supply Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 20 September 2022 · loans signed 25 October 2022 · two treatment plants, 13 groundwater wells, five service reservoirs, 320 km of new water mains
register.note: An older instrument, signed in 2022; to benefit 36,200 households and commercial establishments in Dili
register.text: ADB loans for climate-resilient water infrastructure in Dili and for operational upgrades at the state water utility, Bee Timor-Leste, with regulatory guidelines for the National Authority for Water and Sanitation. It carries the water standard in the capital.

register.name: Australian development assistance, 2026–27
register.detail: Australian Government · total ODA budget estimate 2026–27 · bilateral program A$98.7M · A$135.9M in 2025–26
register.note: Australia describes itself as Timor-Leste’s largest development partner
register.text: Australia’s total official development assistance to Timor-Leste in its 2026–27 development budget. Its programme ensures the continuation of school feeding and vaccination programmes and supports the National Village Development Program (PNDS), whose works include clean water in Aileu; these serve the food, health and water standards.

register.name: Improvement of Guido Valadares National Hospital
register.detail: JICA · grant agreement signed in Dili 20 August 2024 · maximum grant ¥3,093 million · new buildings, medical equipment and consulting services
register.note: The only tertiary-level hospital in Timor-Leste
register.text: A Japanese grant to build and equip the national referral hospital in Dili, to strengthen its capacity to deliver services and the quality of its medical care. It carries the health standard, where the WHO service coverage index stands at 48.

register.name: Financing Sustainable Agriculture in Timor-Leste, credit line to KIF
register.detail: European Investment Bank · approved 15 September 2026 · proposed EIB finance about €10 million · intermediary Kaebauk Investimentu no Finansas SA · credit lines · signature not yet listed
register.note: Women’s economic empowerment is a cross-cutting priority
register.text: A credit line through the microfinance institution Kaebauk Investimentu no Finansas for sustainable agriculture and the blue economy, aimed at underserved rural people, farmers, small traders and micro-enterprises. It serves the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Timor Solar Independent Power Project, Manatuto
register.detail: Announced 27 and 28 July 2026 · JICA loan agreement signed 28 July 2026 · IFC $19M · ADB $12.2M · JICA $12.2M · ADB LEAP2 and CANPA $21.2M · IDA Private Sector Window and IFC Concessional Capital Window $21.2M · MIGA 20-year political risk insurance
register.note: 73.7 MW-AC of solar and 80.2 MWh of battery storage, selling to EDTL under a 25-year power purchase agreement; output equal to the use of about 80,000 households
register.text: The first utility-scale solar and battery storage project in Timor-Leste and its first independent power producer, sponsored by EDF power solutions and I-Environment Investments Pacific, an ITOCHU subsidiary, and run by Manatuto Renewables Power. It carries the energy standard, toward the national goal of meeting 50% of energy needs from renewable sources by 2030.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Petroleum Fund
items.label: Savings from oil and gas, 30 June 2026
items.text: A sovereign fund larger than the economy many times over: the nation’s endowment.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Forest across seven tenths of the land, and coffee grown in its shade.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 33.1% are under fifteen: a young nation with its working life ahead.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2018
items.text: Reefs of the Coral Triangle and mountain trails: a visitor economy still to grow.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: Raw Material
items.text: A social enterprise that works to maximise profits for smallholder coffee farmers, bringing solar-powered wet mills, drying and electric pulpers with battery storage to the off-grid communities of Koileki and Raimutin, with surplus power for household use.

items.name: Cooperativa Café Timor
items.text: A coffee cooperative formed in 2000 that pays farmers guaranteed prices 40 per cent above market prices and hosts seven Clinik Café Timor clinics that provide free health services to smallholder families.

items.name: Pro-ema Restaurant School
items.text: A restaurant school in Dili that teaches culinary skills for careers in the food industry to young people from low-income backgrounds who have faced violence and abuse, within an organisation that also runs a beauty salon and an inn.

items.name: Kaebauk Investimentu no Finansas (KIF)
items.text: A microfinance institution with a loan portfolio of over US$28 million, reaching about 18,464 clients, 58% of them women, with financial services across the country.

items.name: Cooperativa Comercio Agricola de Timor (C-CAT)
items.text: A Fairtrade-certified coffee cooperative whose 1,501 farmer members grow coffee on 2,481.5 hectares, and which has used its Fairtrade Premium to build community water tanks and spring-water systems and buy processing equipment.

items.name: Agora Food Studio
items.text: A gastronomic social enterprise in Dili, co-founded in 2016, whose restaurant and café promote local food and fund the mentoring of local youths to become leaders and entrepreneurs.

items.name: Biojoia de Atauro
items.text: A cooperative on Atauro island formed by hearing-impaired women from impoverished backgrounds, who earn their living making handmade jewellery.

items.name: Boneca de Atauro
items.text: A community-based enterprise on Atauro island, begun in 2006, whose members, 49 women and one boy, make and sell handmade dolls and bags and earn up to US$150 a month in busier months.
